name: Chapter 3 - Money and banking - Comprehensive MCQ Bank

questions.text: In the course, money is defined as wealth that:

options.a: can be used directly to pay for transactions and is generally accepted in the relevant economic environment
options.b: must earn a positive nominal yield
options.c: must be issued only in banknote form
options.d: cannot be held in a bank account

questions.text: Which item is included in money as defined in the chapter?

options.a: overnight/checkable deposits
options.b: a house
options.c: a share of stock that must first be sold

questions.text: The three classical functions of money are:

options.a: means of production, tax base and reserve requirement
options.b: numeraire, GDP deflator and capital stock
options.c: consumption, saving and investment
options.d: unit of account, medium of exchange and store of value

questions.text: If the aggregate price level P rises, the purchasing power of one unit of money, 1/P:

options.a: becomes equal to the nominal interest rate
options.b: rises
options.c: remains exactly constant

questions.text: With positive inflation, the real return on a unit of money with zero nominal yield is:

options.a: equal to the policy rate
options.b: necessarily zero
options.c: positive

questions.text: Why can agents still wish to hold money even though higher-yielding assets exist?

options.a: Money is the only asset whose real value rises with inflation.
options.b: Holding money eliminates all opportunity cost.
options.c: Money provides superior liquidity for transactions.
options.d: Money always has the highest nominal return.

questions.text: An asset is highly liquid when it can be converted into means of payment:

options.a: only after a long maturity, with high fees
options.b: only at an uncertain price
options.c: quickly, with little transaction cost and little uncertainty about nominal value

questions.text: Monetary assets or "quasi-money" are characterized by:

options.a: being physical currency only
options.b: zero yield and perfect direct usability for every transaction
options.c: positive yields and high liquidity, but they may not be directly usable for payments
options.d: no possibility of conversion into money

questions.text: Which ordering correctly reflects the nesting of monetary aggregates?

options.a: M1 = M2 = M3 by definition

questions.text: M1 consists mainly of:

options.a: currency plus all securities regardless of maturity
options.b: only commercial-bank reserves at the central bank
options.c: currency plus overnight/checkable deposits

questions.text: M2 is broader than M1 because it additionally includes:

options.a: all corporate equity
options.b: long-term real estate
options.c: saving deposits and term deposits with maturity up to two years

questions.text: M3 is broader than M2 because it adds, among other things:

options.a: money-market-fund shares and short-maturity debt securities
options.b: government wages
options.c: only physical banknotes

questions.text: The monetary base MB is:

options.a: all loans made by commercial banks
options.b: currency in circulation CH plus commercial-bank reserves R held at the central bank
options.c: M3 minus M2
options.d: currency plus all public deposits D

questions.text: Creation of the monetary base is described as:

options.a: a monopoly of households
options.b: a monopoly of the central bank
options.c: identical to commercial-bank deposit creation

questions.text: Commercial banks create scriptural money primarily through:

options.a: changing the CPI basket
options.b: their credit-granting activity, which creates deposits
options.c: collecting indirect taxes

questions.text: The money supply in the simplified notation is:

options.a: M^s = D − R
options.b: M^s = CH + D
options.c: M^s = CH + R

questions.text: Financial intermediaries transform:

options.a: GDP into the CPI
options.b: taxes into government transfers only
options.c: savings into financing for investment through securities purchases and loans
options.d: currency into physical capital without lending

questions.text: On a commercial bank's simplified balance sheet, reserves held at the central bank are:

options.a: an asset of the commercial bank
options.b: part of household wealth but absent from the bank balance sheet
options.c: a government transfer
options.d: a liability of the commercial bank

questions.text: Demand/checkable deposits held by customers are:

options.a: central-bank assets
options.b: assets of commercial banks
options.c: part of GDP

questions.text: A commercial bank keeps reserves partly to:

options.a: maximize inflation
options.b: finance only long-term government spending
options.c: meet customer cash withdrawals

questions.text: Another reason banks hold reserves is to:

options.a: eliminate all credit risk in the economy
options.b: settle net payments owed to other banks
options.c: ensure every loan is risk-free

questions.text: Reserve requirements imply that banks may have to hold reserves:

options.a: only when interest rates are zero
options.b: in proportion to certain deposits/current accounts
options.c: only in foreign currency
options.d: equal to the full value of all assets

questions.text: On the central bank balance sheet, currency in circulation and commercial-bank reserves are primarily:

options.a: GDP expenditure components
options.b: equity of households
options.c: assets

questions.text: Typical central-bank assets include:

options.a: loans to banks, securities, gold and foreign-exchange reserves
options.b: private consumption goods
options.c: household checkable deposits as liabilities of households

questions.text: An open-market purchase by the central bank generally:

options.a: increases the monetary base by crediting reserve accounts
options.b: reduces banks' reserves one-for-one
options.c: has no balance-sheet effect

questions.text: An open-market sale by the central bank generally:

options.a: increases the monetary base
options.b: decreases the monetary base by debiting reserve accounts
options.c: forces the CPI to fall
options.d: creates household deposits without changing reserves

questions.text: Open-market operations can involve central-bank purchases or sales of:

options.a: only physical capital goods
options.b: only foreign consumer goods
options.c: government bonds, treasury bills or commercial paper

questions.text: In "normal times", the ECB influences reserves using instruments including:

options.a: only tax rates
options.b: only changes in the GDP deflator
options.c: reserve requirements and the conditions/rates on refinancing, marginal lending and deposit facilities

questions.text: The ECB refinancing facility provides reserves to banks through transactions that typically take the form of:

options.a: unsecured gifts
options.b: household tax rebates
options.c: permanent equity purchases in banks

questions.text: In a repo used for refinancing, a bank ultimately:

options.a: converts the loan into GDP
options.b: prints currency to repay the central bank
options.c: buys back the collateral at maturity using reserves
options.d: receives the collateral permanently for free

questions.text: The refinancing rate is a policy rate because it is:

options.a: the return on every long-term bond
options.b: set by household money demand
options.c: set by the ECB rather than determined by market clearing
options.d: equal by definition to the inflation rate

questions.text: The interbank rate is:

options.a: a market rate determined by supply and demand for short-term funds among banks and large financial institutions
options.b: the fixed real interest rate in the Solow model
options.c: a tax rate set by government

questions.text: The marginal lending facility is typically priced:

options.a: below the deposit rate
options.b: above the refinancing rate and therefore acts as an upper bound for the interbank rate
options.c: exactly equal to the GDP growth rate

questions.text: The ECB deposit facility rate typically provides:

options.a: an upper bound for all mortgage rates
options.b: a lower bound for GDP growth
options.c: a lower bound for the interbank rate because banks can place excess reserves at the ECB
options.d: a floor for the inflation rate

questions.text: Quantitative easing (QE) becomes especially relevant when:

options.a: policy rates are already very low and further conventional rate cuts are constrained
options.b: the central bank wants to raise short-term rates rapidly
options.c: the economy has no bonds
options.d: money demand is perfectly inelastic at all rates

questions.text: QE, as described in the slides, involves:

options.a: direct central-bank purchases of bonds on the market
options.b: mandatory increases in reserve requirements only
options.c: direct increases in income taxes
options.d: selling bonds to reduce demand for them

questions.text: By buying bonds under QE, a central bank tends to:

options.a: lower bond prices and raise long-term rates
options.b: leave bond demand unchanged
options.c: increase the real value of currency mechanically through deflation
options.d: raise bond prices and lower longer-term interest rates

questions.text: The slides identify major euro-area QE episodes associated with:

options.a: the 1958 Phillips study and the 1960 Samuelson-Solow study
options.b: the launch of the Belgian CPI
options.c: the sovereign-debt crisis and the COVID-19 outbreak
options.d: the Bretton-Woods conference and the Great Depression

questions.text: The money multiplier is defined as:

options.a: MB / M^s
options.b: M^d / P
options.c: M^s / MB

questions.text: With reserve ratio ρ defined by R = ρD and cash preference c defined by CH = cM^s, the money multiplier is:
Holding cash preference c constant, an increase in the reserve ratio ρ tends to:

options.a: increase the money multiplier
options.b: reduce the money multiplier
options.c: leave the multiplier unchanged

questions.text: Holding ρ constant, a higher cash preference c generally tends to:

options.a: make reserves equal to zero
options.b: have no connection to the money multiplier
options.c: reduce the capacity of a given monetary base to support deposits and therefore lowers the multiplier

questions.text: If c = 0 and ρ = 0.10, the simplified money multiplier equals:
If c = 0.20 and ρ = 0.10, the money multiplier is approximately:
Money demand arises in the chapter mainly because agents:

options.a: always prefer money regardless of interest rates
options.b: cannot hold any other financial assets
options.c: need liquidity for transactions while facing an opportunity cost from forgone interest on other assets
options.d: derive a positive nominal return from currency

questions.text: The money-demand function is represented as:

options.a: M^d = Y/P independent of i
options.b: M^d = P Y L(i), with L decreasing in i
options.c: M^d = P/Y × L(i), with L increasing in i

questions.text: Why does money demand increase with nominal income PY?

options.a: Nominal income is the opportunity cost of money.
options.b: Money demand is assumed proportional only to exports.
options.c: Higher prices and/or higher real activity imply a larger nominal volume of transactions requiring liquidity.
options.d: Higher nominal income lowers the number of transactions.

questions.text: Why does money demand decrease when the nominal interest rate rises?

options.a: Higher rates make money more liquid.
options.b: Higher rates reduce the nominal return on bonds below zero by definition.
options.c: The opportunity cost of holding non-interest-bearing money rises relative to interest-bearing assets.
options.d: Money demand is proportional to the nominal interest rate.

questions.text: At a given money supply, an increase in nominal income PY shifts money demand and tends to:

options.a: raise the equilibrium nominal interest rate
options.b: reduce money supply automatically
options.c: lower the equilibrium nominal interest rate
options.d: leave the interest rate unchanged under the standard downward-sloping money-demand curve

questions.text: At a given nominal income, an increase in money supply tends to:

options.a: raise it
options.b: leave it unchanged except at positive rates
options.c: lower the equilibrium nominal interest rate

questions.text: The standard money-market equilibrium condition is:

options.a: S = I + NX
options.b: M^s = M^d
options.c: Y = C + I only

questions.text: A liquidity trap corresponds to a situation in which:

options.a: money demand becomes highly/perfectly elastic at a very low interest rate, so extra money is willingly held without further lowering the rate
options.b: money demand is vertical and extra money raises rates
options.c: all bonds have infinitely high yields
options.d: the central bank is unable to create reserves

questions.text: At the zero lower bound in the course model, expanding the monetary base through the conventional channel:

options.a: reduces money demand to zero
options.b: must cause immediate hyperinflation
options.c: must raise the short-term rate
options.d: may no longer reduce the short-term interest rate

questions.text: One reason the public is willing to hold additional money in a liquidity trap is that:

options.a: with rates near zero, the opportunity cost of money relative to bonds becomes negligible
options.b: money pays an arbitrarily high nominal return
options.c: bonds become usable directly for every transaction

questions.text: QE provides a way around the conventional zero-lower-bound problem by:

options.a: targeting bond demand and longer-term rates rather than relying only on further cuts in short policy rates
options.b: changing the CPI basket
options.c: raising reserve requirements until money disappears

questions.text: The expected inflation rate formed at t for t+1 is:

options.c: i_t − r_t exactly without approximation in all cases

questions.text: The exact relationship presented before approximation is:

options.a: r_t = i_t + π^e_{t+1} exactly

questions.text: The approximate Fisher relation used in the course is:

options.a: i_t ≈ π^e_{t+1} − r_t
options.b: r_t ≈ i_t/π^e_{t+1}
options.c: r_t ≈ i_t − π^e_{t+1}

questions.text: If the nominal interest rate is 6% and expected inflation is 2%, the approximate real interest rate is:
For a fixed nominal interest rate, higher expected inflation implies:

options.a: a lower real interest rate
options.b: a higher real interest rate
options.c: a lower nominal money supply by identity
options.d: no change in the real rate

questions.text: If expected inflation is zero, then under the Fisher approximation:

options.a: the nominal rate must be zero
options.b: money demand is perfectly elastic
options.c: the real rate is always negative
options.d: the nominal and real interest rates coincide

questions.text: In the money-demand equation, the relevant opportunity-cost interest rate is the:

options.a: real interest rate only
options.b: nominal interest rate
options.c: GDP growth rate

questions.text: Why is the nominal rate the relevant rate for money demand in this model?

options.a: Agents compare nominal transaction balances with the nominal return on alternative financial assets.
options.b: Expected inflation never matters for any decision.
options.c: The central bank cannot affect nominal rates.
options.d: Transactions are measured only in real goods and never in currency.

questions.text: Suppose PY rises while M^s is fixed. In the standard money market, equilibrium is restored by:

options.a: a lower i that further increases money demand
options.b: a higher i that reduces desired money holdings through L(i)
options.c: an automatic fall in P required by accounting identity
options.d: an increase in M^s caused directly by households

questions.text: Suppose the central bank buys securities in an open-market operation and the economy is not in a liquidity trap. The most direct chain is:

options.a: bank reserves ↓ → monetary base ↓ → interest rate ↓
options.b: money demand disappears → prices necessarily fall
options.c: bank reserves ↑ → monetary base ↑ → money supply/liquidity ↑ → equilibrium interest rate tends to ↓
options.d: GDP automatically rises one-for-one with the asset purchase

questions.text: A bank with excess reserves can choose between lending them on the interbank market and placing them at the ECB. This helps explain why the ECB deposit rate is:

options.a: irrelevant for reserve allocation
options.b: equal to the inflation rate
options.c: a floor for the interbank rate
options.d: a ceiling for the interbank rate

questions.text: A bank facing a reserve shortage can borrow overnight through the marginal lending facility. This helps explain why the marginal lending rate is:

options.a: a floor for the interbank rate
options.b: a ceiling for the interbank rate
options.c: necessarily below the deposit rate

questions.text: (Select the incorrect answer) In the chapter's simplified monetary system:

options.a: the central bank controls the monetary base
options.b: commercial banks can create deposits through lending
options.c: commercial banks have the monopoly over creation of the monetary base
options.d: money supply includes currency and deposits
